_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band3_the_river_lock. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 3000-3999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.
_comment_why_this_was_empty: GATE-D3. This file existed with an empty `clusters` array -- nothing built anywhere in 1580m of river country. tether_relay.json's own `_comment_props` invited exactly this: 'The site's loose gear ... belongs in data/config/props.json as a `relay_station` cluster ... That cluster is not authored yet.' The four clusters below are that invitation plus the region's other two missing beats: Team Tether presence building on the approach BEFORE the pickets (prompt 64: 'The route should not jump from wilderness directly into the four-person relay gauntlet'), and the mill/crossing structures §3 Band 3 asks the river region to read as a landmark rather than decorative terrain. Every model is one the settlement already uses (D24, one prop family) -- nothing here is new.

clusters.name: riverwatch_rest
clusters._why: GATE-D3, the region's camp/rest siting (prompt 64: 'a reasonable recovery/staging point before or around the relay approach should exist'). Sited on the flattest ground measured anywhere in the band (vegetation.json order 3000, 0.35m of spread over an 8m box), right past the spine's bend into the relay road and well short of either picket. Deliberately NOT a healer or a second camp mechanic -- the game has exactly one rest structure (scripts/build/camp.gd) and this is not a second one. What stands here is evidence a traveller already used this spot: a seat, a set-down pack, a water barrel. It reads as an obvious place to plant your own camp before pushing into Team Tether ground, not as a free-heal station inside the gauntlet.

props._why: the cluster's anchor -- somewhere to sit before the approach
water, kept within reach of the bench
set down against the bench leg, not merely near it -- the same 'touching pile reads as one load' rule the quarry and ranger-camp clusters already use

GATE-D3 round 2. The blind critic read this spot as 'a prop dropped into a field rather than somewhere anyone has stayed' -- three objects on untouched grass with nothing that says a night was spent here. This is the piece that says it. A bedroll left behind is also the honest read for a staging point that is NOT a rest mechanic: the game has exactly one rest structure (scripts/build/camp.gd) and this is still not a second one, it is evidence the last traveller through slept here before pushing into Team Tether ground
left by the bench with the firewood it cut. Two pieces of evidence of work beat one, and an axe set down is the cheapest thing in this kit that reads as an interrupted human activity
the fourth corner of the group, closing it into a camp with a middle rather than a line of objects along the road

clusters.name: relay_approach_checkpoint
clusters._why: GATE-D3. The first physical sign of Team Tether on the road, well short of Hess -- a barricade rather than a person, because a fight here would just be a third picket and prompt 64 asks for presence BUILDING before the gauntlet, not another battle. At s=12.5m along the (230,3670)->(350,3760) spine leg, 10m short of Hess at s=22.5 so the two do not compete for the player's stopping point.
clusters._why_rebuilt: GATE-D3 round 2, and it is two defects in one cluster. The driven run (tools/_probe_band3_driven.gd) WEDGED the real player body here: the crate and barrel stood 0.4m and 1.2m from the spine centreline, so a body walking the road pushed straight into them for ninety frames and stopped. Three props dropped on the walking line of the region's main road. Second, the blind critic was shown this spot and said plainly that nothing here reads as a picket -- two identical crates on a path, no camp, no barrier, no reason. Both are answered the same way: the barricade is now a LINE ACROSS the road with a 6.4m gap walked through the middle of it, and the picket's own camp sits off the verge behind it. A checkpoint you steer through reads as a checkpoint; a checkpoint you get stuck on reads as a bug. Every lateral offset below is measured on that leg's own normal (-0.6,0.8), so the gap stays a gap if the road is ever re-cut.

props._why: west end of the barricade, 3.2m off the centreline and squared to the road rather than to the world -- yaw 36.9 is the leg's own bearing, so the crate face reads as blocking the road instead of sitting at an accident of an angle
set against the crate, one load, further out
the west line run out to 6.4m so the barricade has length -- two crates read as luggage, a line of three reads as something put there on purpose

east end, the mirror of the west crate. The 6.4m the two leave between them is the gap the road walks through: wide enough that a body steers it without touching either, narrow enough that the player is obviously being funnelled
east line, second piece
a cordon line run along the east barricade rather than coiled on the road -- the closest this pack's catalog comes to a barrier marker, and lying along the line it now has one to lie along

the picket's own camp, 8m off the verge behind the east barricade and facing back down the road at whoever is coming. This is the piece the critic's 'no camp, no reason' asks for: somebody sits here and watches this road
kit set down against the bench leg -- the same touching-pile rule riverwatch_rest uses
water at the watch post. Three pieces make it a post rather than a bench nobody uses

clusters.name: relay_station
clusters._why: GATE-D3, adopting tether_relay.json's own open invitation (`_comment_props`): the site's loose gear, placed inside the compound yard rather than duplicated in that file. Positions are the site's own (s,t) local frame (tether_relay.json's `_frame`) converted to world metres -- s around -7..-9 (just inside the gate, off the road axis every fight stands on) so the crates sit in the yard corner rather than in the walk line between Hess/Orrin/Dell and the console.

props._why: the anchor -- requisitioned stock, still crated
against the first crate's side, one load
a second stack, a couple of paces off -- the yard has an edge instead of a boundary
left leaning near the gate, the excavation tool that dug the spoil the burrowback cluster now lives in
near the pad's foot -- somebody's kit, the detail that makes the site occupied rather than merely built

clusters.name: old_mill_crossing_gear
clusters._why: GATE-D3, spec's own 'mill/crossing structures' beat. mill_crossing.gd and terrain_playground.json's `crossings[old_mill_crossing]` already build the deck, the channel and the gate logic -- this is the loose gear around it, the same treatment the quarry's working face gets: tools left where the crew stopped, which is also the honest reason a bridge missing one gear (data/dialogue/relay.json's `relay_captive_freed`) reads as abandoned rather than never-finished.
clusters._why_resited: GATE-D3 round 2. This cluster was authored at (-60,4160): 101m from the Old Mill Crossing it is named for and 54m off the spine, dressing nothing and seen by nobody. The driven run never came within reach of it and the blind critic, shown the crossing, said the mill stands alone on bare ground with no yard, no track and no reason -- both are the same defect. It now stands on the SOUTH bank landing where the player actually stops at a shut gate, 13-17m short of the narrows: the channel is 15m deep with a 3.6m half-width and a 3.4m rim, and terrain_playground.json fades the carve out to z=4191, so everything below sits at z<=4189 and never hangs over a cut edge. Laterally it is 4-5m off the road centreline (x=-152), on the verges, because the wedge this same run found at the relay checkpoint was three props standing on the walking line and that mistake is not worth making twice.

props._why: the anchor -- spare deck timber, crated, on the west verge of the landing where a crew working the bridge would stack it
coiled rigging line for the deck, set down against the crate
tipped a couple of paces off -- the group has an edge, not a boundary

the east verge, facing the narrows. The gate is shut because the mechanism is missing a gear, and a bench turned toward the work is what says somebody was in the middle of fixing it when Team Tether took the person who knew how
beside the bench -- mill gearing is iron, and this is the pack's only piece that says iron was worked here
closes the east group at three pieces, matching the west

clusters.name: old_mill_yard
clusters._why_regrouped: GATE-D3 round 3. Round 2's version put five pieces at five separate spots across an open apron, and the critic read exactly that back: 'nothing grouped into a working area, nothing pointed at anything else... a mill yard should have material staged where the mill needs it.' Regrouped into one loading face 4-8m off the mill's own south-east corner, crates touching, barrel closing the stack, bench and bucket turned toward the door. The whole group now spans 4m instead of 8m and every piece faces the building it serves.
clusters._why: GATE-D3 round 2, and it exists because of one specific piece of blind criticism: shown the Old Mill Crossing, the critic said the half-timbered mill 'stands alone on a bare hilltop on a stone plinth, with no path to its door, no fence, no outbuilding, no garden' -- a prop dropped on grass rather than a place someone worked. The mill itself is built by mill_crossing.gd from the crossing's own `mill` block and is not this file's to move; what it has never had is a yard. This is that yard: the working clutter of a water mill, on the north bank clear of the mill's own footprint and well clear of the channel carve (everything at z>=4218, against a fade that ends at 4215). Same prop family as every other cluster in the region (D24) -- no new models.

props._why: grain in, flour out: a mill's yard is stacked with what it is milling, and a filled crate says the place worked recently rather than being a ruin
emptied and re-stacked beside the full one, the pair reading as a load part-worked
set out from the crates so the yard has depth instead of being one touching pile
turned toward the mill door -- the yard's one human-scale object, and the thing that makes the group read as somewhere people sat rather than storage
water from the race, left at the bench end
